issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate, but the template defines a function with a different name (create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate). This name mismatch is structural: students following the template will search for create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate (as described in the problem and used in the solution/tests) but will not find it in the template, causing confusion and import/usage errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate to match the problem statement and solution (and any tests), or update the problem statement and solution to use create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate consistently. Ensure the function signature and docstring remain the same.

issues.description: The tensor-networks task and solution refer to a function named create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate, but the template implements a function named create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate. This names the same conceptual entity (a nearest-neighbor / adjacent two-qubit gate tensor) with two different identifiers, which can confuse students mapping the problem statement to the template and cause failures when tests expect the name from the problem/solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate (and update any internal references and docstrings) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier. Alternatively, update the problem statement and tests to reference create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate, but prefer aligning the template name with the problem/solution.
